leads.title: Pennington v. Government - U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
leads.documents: Only reported sodomy case in Guam (early 1950s); defendant accused of sodomy won on procedural grounds, court held trial court lacked authority to try without jury. Documents historical criminalization enforcement.

leads.title: Ruling by Chief Judge Frances Tydingco-Gatewood, U.S. District Court for the District of Guam - June 5, 2015
leads.documents: Held Guam's prohibition on same-sex couples marrying unconstitutional; led to issuance of marriage licenses 4 days later. Documents marriage equality legal status.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text. Citation detail visible: June 5, 2015 ruling, Chief Judge Frances Tydingco-Gatewood, District of Guam.

leads.title: Latta v. Otter - U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
leads.documents: Ninth Circuit decision striking down identical same-sex marriage bans in Idaho and Nevada, cited as precedent for Guam marriage ruling. Documents federal appellate rights machinery.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text. Citation detail visible: 'Latta v. Otter' cited in Tydingco-Gatewood decision.

leads.title: Guam Marriage Equality Act of 2015 - Legislature of Guam
leads.documents: Passed August 11, 2015 making Guam marriage laws gender-neutral after court ruling. Documents statutory recognition of same-sex relationships.

leads.documents: Unanimously passed August 2015 banning discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity or expression in employment, including government employees. Documents employment protections.

leads.title: Senator Fernando Esteves transgender legal gender change bill - Legislature of Guam
leads.documents: May 2018 bill to allow legal gender change via judicial permission plus letter from psychologist/social worker/therapist without surgery requirement; postponed Dec 13, 2018 and defeated 6-7 Dec 17, 2018. Documents current surgery requirement for birth certificate/driver's license change.
leads.detail: No URL visible in provided text. Citation detail visible: introduced May 2018 by Sen. Fernando Esteves, defeated 6-7 on Dec 17, 2018; current rule requires physician sworn statement of sex reassignment surgery to Office of Vital Statistics / Motor Vehicle Division Supervisor.

leads.documents: Poll of Guam residents: 55% in favor of same-sex marriage, 29% opposed, 16% undecided. Documents social attitudes/living conditions context.
